children: The investment will fund four projects across Oman and Odisha, with operations planned between 2027 and 2029

Brookfield will invest up to $600 million in ACME Cleantech Ventures, a UK-based privately held entity within the ACME Group, to support the development of ACME's green molecule projects in India and West Asia, the global investment firm said on Thursday.

The investment is being made through Brookfield Global Transition Fund, which focuses on investments in net-zero carbon opportunities. The funding will be used to develop projects involving green molecules such as green hydrogen, ammonia and methanol, which are produced using zero-carbon energy.

According to ACME Group chairman Manoj Upadhyay, the investment is structured as an equity deal. The capital will be used to fund four projects — Oman Phase 2, two green ammonia projects and a green methanol project in Odisha. The equity valuation is expected to be decided by the end of 2026.
ACME will retain a significant majority stake in its projects and business entities, Upadhyay said.

ACME currently has an operational green ammonia facility in Bikaner, Rajasthan, and is developing a green ammonia project in Duqm, Oman. It is also establishing green ammonia and green methanol facilities in Odisha.

The company's Odisha projects include a green ammonia facility being developed under a Green Ammonia Purchase Agreement with the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI), along with a strategic joint venture (JV) with Japan's IHI Corporation.

ACME has also entered into offtake agreements with international and domestic companies, including Yara International and Indian fertiliser companies IFFCO, Paradeep Phosphates, Coromandel International and Indorama India.

The company said Phase 1 of its Oman project is fully funded and is expected to become operational by March 2027. The green ammonia project in Paradeep, Odisha, and the green methanol project are expected to be operational in 2028, while the ACME-IHI JV green ammonia project is expected to be operational in 2029.

Brookfield said the investment marks its entry into the green molecules sector in the region. Brookfield has more than $1 trillion in assets under management and an energy portfolio comprising approximately 50 gigawatt of wind and solar assets in operation and under development in India.
